# restic 0.17.3, restore ID:/volumes/vx --target T --include PATTERN, where the
# snapshot holds /volumes/vx/a.txt, /volumes/vx/empty/, /volumes/vx/sub/b.txt
# and /volumes/vx/sub/deep/c.txt: a pattern is relative to the folder restored.
/volumes/vx/sub	nothing
/sub	sub sub/b.txt sub/deep sub/deep/c.txt
sub	sub sub/b.txt sub/deep sub/deep/c.txt
sub/b.txt	sub sub/b.txt
/volumes/vx/sub/b.txt	nothing
# restore ID --target T, all of the snapshot: a pattern is the snapshot's path.
/volumes/vx/sub	volumes volumes/vx volumes/vx/sub volumes/vx/sub/b.txt volumes/vx/sub/deep volumes/vx/sub/deep/c.txt
/sub	nothing
# globs: restore ID:/volumes/vx --target T --include PATTERN, where the snapshot
# holds, in /volumes/vx, file[1].txt, file1.txt, data*, datax, a[b, q?, qa, x\y,
# xy, d[1]/in/c.txt, d1/e.txt, b] and b. Each name of a pattern is a glob, and a
# backslash makes the character after it stand for itself; a pattern that is no
# glob fails the restore, exit code 1.
/file[1].txt	file1.txt
/file\[1].txt	file[1].txt
/data*	data* datax
/data\*	data*
/a[b	error: Fatal: --include: invalid pattern(s) provided:
/a\[b	a[b
/q?	q? qa
/q\?	q?
/x\y	xy
/x\\y	x\y
/d[1]	d1 d1/e.txt
/d\[1]	d[1] d[1]/in d[1]/in/c.txt
/d\[1]/in/c.txt	d[1] d[1]/in d[1]/in/c.txt
/b]	b]
